note: Provenance register. Every number published by the site traces to one of these entries. 'official' means a page published by the National Football League; 'mirror' means a third-party redistribution that this project had to use for bulk data because the sandbox can only reach github.com, codeload.github.com, api.github.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org and npmjs.org, plus the page-fetch tool for nfl.com.

official.used_for: Official authority for every team's W-L-T, points for and points against in 2025. 32 rows cross-checked against results computed from the game-level data.

official.name: NFL.com — 2026 League Standings (regular season, through the games completed on 2026-11-01)
official.used_for: Same verification for the in-progress 2026 season (32 rows).

official.used_for: Player-prop game log and season total (SEA WR). Weekly values sum to the published season total.

official.used_for: Prop game log (GB WR); pairs with Jordan Love for the quarterback/receiver correlation.

official.used_for: Prop game log (GB QB); pairs with Christian Watson.

official.name: NFL.com — 2026 player-stats category pages (passing / rushing / receiving)
official.used_for: Selecting WHICH players to capture. No statistic from these pages is published: the text extraction drops the column headers, so any label would be a guess. See irregularity I6.

mirror.name: nflverse/nfldata — open data mirror (games, closing lines, teams, standings)
mirror.used_for: Every game result, rest day, roof/surface, temperature and wind value, and every closing spread / total / moneyline in the backtests and on the originated board.
mirror.trust_evidence: The mirror's game results reproduce the official NFL standings exactly for all 32 teams in both 2025 and 2026 (64/64 team-seasons, 77/77 checks). See verification.html.
mirror.caveat: Closing lines are a third-party record of sportsbook prices. They are not a league publication and were not independently re-verified against a sportsbook; see irregularity I8.

mirror.name: nflverse/nflverse-data — weekly player and team statistics releases
mirror.used_for: Attempted ingestion of game-level player statistics for a full prop backtest.
mirror.caveat: Release assets redirect to release-assets.githubusercontent.com, which this sandbox cannot reach (TLS refused). No player file from this source was ingested; see irregularity I3.

unavailable.name: Any player-prop price (e.g. a sportsbook or odds aggregator)
unavailable.effect: Prop strategies cannot be settled against a real market. They are published with a -110 assumption, blocked by the sample gate, and marked 'needs review'.

unavailable.name: NFL rulebook (attempted https://www.nfl.com/the-rules/)
unavailable.effect: No rule text is quoted anywhere in this project. The correlation work is empirical, not rule-derived.

unavailable.name: Opening lines for the modern era
unavailable.status: present, but only 2021 and 1,088 rows from a single book (data/initial_lines.csv)
unavailable.effect: No opening-to-closing (line-movement) strategy was tested; only closing prices are used.

assumptions.assumption: Spread and total legs settle at -110 (decimal 1.9091).
assumptions.why: The mirror stores closing prices only for moneylines; the two-way spread/total market is conventionally priced at -110.
assumptions.impact: All non-moneyline ROI numbers scale linearly with this price.

assumptions.assumption: Flat 1-unit stakes, no line shopping, no bet limits, no vig rebates.
assumptions.impact: Real-world ROI after shopping would differ.

assumptions.assumption: The closing line is the price taken.
assumptions.why: It is the only price in the data.
assumptions.impact: A bettor who must play earlier would face different numbers.

assumptions.assumption: Leaderboard rewards are virtual points and badges, not money.
assumptions.why: This is a skill competition, not a wagering product.

irregularities.finding: nflverse `spread_line` sign convention disagrees with its own documentation.
irregularities.detail: nflfastR documentation describes +7.5 as the home team being a 7.5-point underdog. In this file the opposite holds: over 108 completed 2026 games, corr(spread_line, home_moneyline) = -0.976 and corr(spread_line, home_margin) = +0.334, i.e. a positive value means the HOME team is favoured. The pipeline therefore uses the empirical convention and build_dataset.py fails loudly if the correlation ever flips.

irregularities.finding: Two different club abbreviations for Arizona.
irregularities.detail: nfl.com prints 'AZ'; the mirror prints 'ARI'. An explicit alias map is applied before comparing (also LAR->LA, OHSH->WAS, JAC->JAX and relocations).
irregularities.resolution: Alias map in scripts/verify_official.py; no rows dropped.

irregularities.finding: Weekly player/team statistics releases are unreachable, so the prop sample is tiny.
irregularities.detail: Every nflverse-data release asset redirects to release-assets.githubusercontent.com and the TLS handshake is refused from this sandbox. Prop work therefore rests on six hand-captured nfl.com game logs (41 player-games) instead of a full season of game-level data.
irregularities.resolution: Prop strategies are published but blocked by gate G1 (sample) and marked 'needs review'.

irregularities.finding: No player-prop prices anywhere in reach.
irregularities.detail: Prop ROI uses the -110 assumption (A2). No edge is claimed for any prop.
irregularities.resolution: Flagged; prop rows carry no rank.

irregularities.finding: NFL.com does not publish betting lines, so 'our line vs the market' compares against a third-party record of sportsbook closes.
irregularities.detail: The market column comes from the nflverse mirror, not from the league.

irregularities.finding: NFL.com player-stats category pages lose their column headers in text extraction.
irregularities.detail: Rows arrive as bare number sequences whose order cannot be proven, so publishing a 'receiving yards' value from those pages would be a guess. They are used only to pick players, never as a value source.
irregularities.resolution: Values come from each player's own page, where every column has a printed header.

irregularities.finding: The mirror snapshot is mid-round for 2026 Week 8.
irregularities.detail: 108 of 272 scheduled 2026 regular-season games were complete at capture (through the Thursday Week 8 game). Week 8 is therefore excluded from the published board and only Weeks 9 and 10 are originated.
One mirror, no independent sportsbook cross-check. A stale or mis-keyed price would propagate into every ROI figure.
irregularities.resolution: Accepted with disclosure; totals/spreads still reproduce every official game result.

irregularities.finding: Game-page URLs verified only for a subset of fixtures.
irregularities.detail: The page-fetch tool returned the Week 8 and Week 9 schedule pages in chunks; eight Week 9 game-page URLs were seen verbatim and are stored. Every other board row links to the official weekly schedule page instead of a constructed URL, so no dead link is published.
irregularities.resolution: Rows fall back to the verified weekly page.

irregularities.detail: The rulebook URL this project would have used returns a 404 from nfl.com, and no rule text was independently verified, so no rule is quoted.
irregularities.resolution: Rules removed from the analysis entirely.
